title: Italian Navy’s First ‘Full’ PPA Giovanni delle Bande Nere Demonstrates BMD Capabilities
zh_title: 意大利海军首艘“完整”PPA Giovanni delle Bande Nere 展示弹道导弹防御能力
summary: 在意大利海军 BMD 的一个重大里程碑中，第一艘“全”MPCS/PPA Giovanni delle Bande Nere 使用 Aster 30 拦截了一枚高速弹道导弹。Giovanni delle Bande Nere (P 434) 是 Thaon di Revel 级的第四艘单位，也是第一艘 MPCS/PPA（多用途战斗舰/Pattugliatore Polivalente d’Altura），由 Fincantieri 建造并交付莱昂纳多的“PPA Full”多角色配置具有增强型综合防空和导弹防御（IAMD）以及反潜战能力，是意大利海军成功实现自主作战的首要作战平台
content:
在意大利海军 BMD 的一个重大里程碑中，第一艘“全”MPCS/PPA Giovanni delle Bande Nere 使用 Aster 30 拦截了一枚高速弹道导弹。Giovanni delle Bande Nere (P 434) 是 Thaon di Revel 级的第四艘单位，也是第一艘 MPCS/PPA（多用途战斗舰/Pattugliatore Polivalente d’Altura），由 Fincantieri 建造并交付据意大利海军社交媒体报道，“PPA Full”多角色配置具有增强的综合防空和导弹防御（IAMD）以及莱昂纳多的反潜作战能力，是意大利海军的首要作战平台，可在实弹射击过程中成功实现从探测到拦截“高速弹道导弹”的自主交战。 Bande Nere 最近完成了在印度-太平洋地区为期六个月的作战部署，并于 2026 年 11 月 13 日返回其位于塔兰托海军基地的母港。这一成就使 Marina Militare 跻身能够直接应对海上弹道威胁的海军俱乐部之列。 Bande Nere MPCS/PPA Full已在印太地区进行了为期六个月的作战部署，参加了环太平洋军演和太平洋龙2026演习。 （美国海军摄影：大众传播专家一级 Erik Melgar）“多任务战舰 Giovanni delle Bande Nere 成功地进行了一次高度复杂的演习，探测、拦截和压制高速弹道导弹。
11 月 20 日，意大利海军在其 X 社交媒体账户上表示：“成功的链条包括：精确探测和跟踪、使用舰载作战管理系统计算发射解决方案、交战和完美拦截。”该公告还附有从 Bande Nere MPCS/PPA 快速连发两枚 MBDA Aster 防空导弹进行实弹射击的视频，以及操作员在作战作战中心控制台上的图像。尽管目前尚未提供有关实弹射击的更多细节，但据报道，根据《海军新闻》收集的信息和 CMS 控制台上显示的地图，“班德尼尔”号船员在过去几周内在希腊克里特岛的北约导弹发射装置（NAMFI）海上射击场进行了现场交战，据知情人士透露，这项活动是由意大利海军 MPCS/PPA 船员在去年 11 月 13 日抵达其母港之前进行的，当时是在印度-太平洋地区进行了六个月的作战部署返回途中。 《海军新闻》了解到，如此高要求的实弹射击演习并不是在“内雷号”号于2026年5月出发执行作战部署之前计划的，而是在任务期间安排和准备的，进一步证实了意大利海军在快速变化的作战环境中规划和应对紧急作战需求的灵活性。
意大利海上防御和国家科技工业的非凡作战成就！这一成功立即将 #MarinaMilitare 打造成一支能够直接对抗海上弹道威胁的海军陆战队精锐部队，保证…… pic.twitter.com/46MWq5FjXD — Marina Militare (@ItalianNavy) 2026 年 11 月 20 日 自 Fincantieri 于 10 月交付以来，第一艘全战斗配置的 PPA 接受了对具有 IAMD 和多角色能力的新战斗和武器系统套件的广泛资格和操作评估

【原文 English Original】
In a major Italian Navy BMD milestone, the first ‘Full’ MPCS/PPA Giovanni delle Bande Nere intercepted a high-speed ballistic missile using Aster 30. The Giovanni delle Bande Nere (P 434), the fourth unit of the Thaon di Revel-class and the first MPCS/PPA (Multi-Purpose Combat Ship/Pattugliatore Polivalente d’Altura) built by Fincantieri and delivered in the “PPA Full” multi-role configuration with enhanced integrated air and missile defence (IAMD) alongside anti-submarine warfare capabilities by Leonardo, is the premiere combatant platform of the Italian Navy to achieve a successful autonomous engagement from detection to interception of a ‘high-speed ballistic missile’ during a live firing, according to Italian Navy social media. The Bande Nere has recently completed its six-month operational deployment in the Indo-Pacific region, with the return to its homeport at Taranto naval base on 13 November 2026. This achievement places the Marina Militare among the club of navies capable of countering ballistic threats directly from the sea. The Bande Nere MPCS/PPA Full has conducted a six-month operational deployment in the Indo-Pacific region participating to RIMPAC and PACIFIC DRAGON 2026 exercises. (U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Erik Melgar) “The multi-mission combat vessel Giovanni delle Bande Nere successfully conducted a highly complex exercise, detecting, intercepting and neutralising a high-speed ballistic missile. The chain of success: precision detection and tracking, calculation of the firing solution using the onboard Combat Management System, engagement and flawless interception,” said the Italian Navy with her X social media account on 20 November. The announcement was accompanied by a video of the live firing with a ‘ripple’ of two MBDA Aster air defence missiles in rapid sequence from the Bande Nere MPCS/PPA alongside images of operators at their consoles in the combat operational centre. Although no further details were provided so far about the live firing, according to information collected by Naval News and the maps displayed on the CMS consoles, the live engagement was conducted by the Bande Nere crew in the last couple of weeks on the at-sea firing range area of the NATO Missile Firing Installation (NAMFI) on the island of Crete in Greece. This activity, according to informed sources was carried out by the Italian Navy MPCS/PPA crew before reaching its homeport last 13 November, on the way back from the six-month operational deployment in the Indo-Pacific region. Naval News understood that such demanding live firing exercise wasn’t planned before the departure of the Bande Nere for the operational deployment in May 2026, but was scheduled and prepared during the mission, further confirming the Italian Navy planning flexibility and response to urgent operational needs in a fast changing operational environment. Un traguardo operativo straordinario per la difesa marittima italiana e per l'industria tecnologica nazionale! Questo successo proietta da subito la #MarinaMilitare in un'élite ristretta di Marine capaci di contrastare minacce balistiche direttamente dal mare, garantendo la… pic.twitter.com/46MWq5FjXD — Marina Militare (@ItalianNavy) November 20, 2026 The first PPA in the full combat configuration was subjected to an extensive qualification and operational evaluation of the new combat and weapon system suite with IAMD and multirole capabilities since its delivery by Fincantieri in October 2024. The Bande Nere launched its first Aster 30 missile in February 2025 and participated to the international IAMD Formidable Shield followed by the French Navy-lead Polaris exercises in the Atlantic Ocean in the same year, before conducting the six-month operational deployment in the Indo-Pacific region in 2026. Here, it joined the US Navy-lead RIMPAC worldwide largest naval exercise and the IAMD-dedicated Pacific Dragon exercise. According to the information released by the Italian Navy social media and the associated video, the Bande Nere crew successfully employed the ship combat system centred on the Leonardo SADOC 5 CMS with IAMD capabilities and the Dual Band Radar (DBR) incorporating the four fixed-faces (4FF) AESA GaN-based C-band Kronos Quad and the 4FF AESA X-band GaAs-based Star Fire systems, alongside the integrated electronic warfare suite (IEWS) by ELT Group, to detect, track and generate the firing solution to successfully engaged the ballistic target with the MBDA Italia SAAM ESD (Surface Anti-Air Missile – Extended Self Defence) PPA air defence missile system. Centred on two Naval Group A50 8-cell vertical launch systems (VLS) for the family of Aster surface-to-air munitions, C2 and firing units, the SAAM ESD PPA system launched a ‘ripple’ of two Aster 30 missiles to intercept and successfully neutralize the ballistic threat. No indication was provided on the missile type, but the longer range Aster 30 is used for the ATBM mission as identified by the video still frames. Based on previous information released on the contracts and deliveries of Aster 30 munitions to Italian Navy, Naval News understood the Bande Nere MPCS/PPA employed the standard Aster 30 munition, which represents the inventory weapon for the Italian Navy. If officially confirmed, it represent a further testimony of the Aster 30 capabilities against ballistic threats, after the first engagements conducted in 2024 by the French Navy in the Red Sea. This until both Navies will receive the Aster 30 Block 1 NT munition version specifically developed to counter ballistic as well as hypersonic missile threats in addition to conventional ones including aircraft, drones and cruise missiles. An operator at a console of the Leonardo SADOC 4 CMS of the Bande Nere MPCS/PPA during the live firing at the NAMFI at-sea range area. (Photo credit: Italian Navy) “An extraordinary operational milestone for Italian maritime defence and the national industry. This success places the Marina Militare among an elite group of navies capable of countering ballistic threats directly from the sea, ensuring the stability and security of maritime routes in the Mediterranean and beyond,” highlighted the Italian Navy with the same statement on its X social media account. No further information were released on the firing theme and used ballistic target, but according to the NAMFI website, anti-tactical ballistic missile (ATBM) firings are the most important an demanding activities conducted on the international military range managed by the Hellenic Ministry of Defence, since the firsts were carried out by German and Netherlands Air Defence Units at the same facilities on October 2007, being an European first. Besides such land-based activities, which are conducted in support of Patriot ground based air defence systems, NAMFI range has the capability and experience to also host naval (platform) firings against ballistic missile targets, as demonstrated by the successful activities of the Italian Navy MPCS/PPA. The ATBM firings are conducted for the air defence units “against the Supersonic Target (STAR) missile provided by TMD target company, according to NAMFI website. Naval News understood the target was fired from a land site, while the ship was operating in high sea inside the at-sea wide range area. The NAMFI range includes a 14,440 square kilometres of land, sea and air space with an area at sea 166 km long and 87 km wide (expandable to 226 km in length under certain conditions for a total of 19,660 square kilometres) which stretches along the northern coast of Crete island. This area is divided in 3 subareas (A, B and C), it is crossed by air corridors, it affects two international airport terminals (Heraklion and Chania) and four main national ports (Souda, Rethimno, Heraklion, Santorini). The successful autonomous engagement of a target representing a tactical ballistic missile not only adds the Italian Navy to the club of naval forces capable of defending the national territory, fleet and allied ships against this threats but also testimony the capabilities reached by the Italian defence and naval industry in the IAMD sector. The combat and weapon system of the MPCS/PPA in the full combat configuration is planned to equip the whole class of ships as well as the FREEM EVO platform and and are offered on the international market, where the launch customer is expected to be the Portuguese MoD and Navy with the national FREMM EVO procurement programme, but thanks to its scalability and modularity can be integrated on other naval platforms offered by Fincantieri but also other shipbuilders. The post Italian Navy’s First ‘Full’ PPA Giovanni delle Bande Nere Demonstrates BMD Capabilities appeared first on Naval News .

title: China’s conspicuous absence in Asian energy security plans
zh_title: 中国在亚洲能源安全计划中明显缺席
summary: 中国在亚洲能源安全计划中明显缺席 - 大西洋理事会中国 东亚 能源与环境 地缘政治与能源安全 2026 年 11 月 25 日 • 东部时间上午 10:04 中国在亚洲能源安全计划中明显缺席 霍尔木兹海峡冲击发生九个月后，能源安全已被列入上周日本-东盟和亚太经合组织 (APEC) 峰会的议程。五年来的第二次价格冲击迫使亚洲政策制定者重新考虑能源安全规划和机构，但中国并没有带头，尽管它在地区能源领域发挥着重要作用。
content:
大西洋理事会：亚洲能源安全计划中明显缺席中国
中国东亚 能源与环境 地缘政治与能源安全
2026 年 11 月 25 日 • 上午 10:04（美国东部时间）
中国在亚洲能源安全计划中明显缺席
霍尔木兹海峡地震发生九个月后，能源安全问题被提上上周日本-东盟和亚太经济合作组织 (APEC) 峰会的议程。五年来的第二次价格冲击迫使亚洲政策制定者重新考虑能源安全规划和机构，但中国并没有带头，尽管它在地区能源安全中发挥着重要作用。
中国的优先事项是国内而非地区
作为世界上最大的石油进口国，中国与经历霍尔木兹海峡供应中断的邻国依赖进口的国家有很多共同点。然而，新兴的关于新的合作能源安全规划机制和机构的区域政策讨论基本上没有提及这一点。
在过去的八个月里，中国一直专注于国内能源优先事项，其行为有时会损害其他亚洲进口国。美国和以色列袭击伊朗仅一周后，中国就禁止了几乎所有石油产品的出口许可证。中国在随后几个月放松了这些限制，但在柴油和其他燃料库存大幅下降后，十月份北京再次限制产品出口。
中国只是东亚第三大石油产品出口国（仅次于韩国和新加坡），但其出口配额的意外变化改变了市场平衡。例如，2025 年，中国供应了澳大利亚近三分之一的航空燃油进口，因此 3 月份的航空燃油禁令让澳大利亚航空公司纷纷寻找替代品。
更广泛地说，中国缺乏透明度给邻国带来了挑战。其2025年至2026年3月的库存增加支撑了全球石油需求，而炼油厂开工率下降、国内燃料价格上限和出口限制等综合因素导致2月至6月原油进口出现前所未有的下降。分析师指出，中国在石油市场的定价能力源于其原油购买的时间和数量。然而，虽然国内考虑推动了这些决定，但它们往往让中国的邻国围绕其行动进行规划。尽管宣布建立东盟-中国能源合作伙伴关系，但其邻国有理由对中国的承诺持谨慎态度。
在经历了能源危机最初几个月的急剧下降之后，亚洲石油进口已经反弹。但这次中断影响了所有依赖中东石油和天然气的进口商。日本通常 90% 以上的原油从中东进口，因此被迫从美国或拉丁美洲寻找替代品（9 月份，美国原油占日本进口量的 27%，高于去年的 3%）。通常从中东进口大部分液化石油气的印度已转向美国供应。其他亚洲进口商一直在努力获取石化原料。
进口商正在重新评估他们的供应商关系。正如国际能源署 (IEA) 执行董事法提赫·比罗尔 (Fatih Birol) 在 2026 年 4 月大西洋理事会活动中所说，进口商现在有三个重要目标：“能源来源多元化。能源结构多元化。贸易路线多元化。”对于长期依赖石油的亚洲进口商来说，这是一项艰巨的任务。

China’s conspicuous absence in Asian energy security plans - Atlantic Council
China East Asia Energy & Environment Geopolitics & Energy Security
November 25, 2026 • 10:04am ET
China’s conspicuous absence in Asian energy security plans
Nine months into the Strait of Hormuz shock, energy security was on the agenda at last week’s Japan-ASEAN and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summits. The second price shock in five years has forced Asian policymakers to rethink energy security planning and institutions—but China is not leading the charge despite its significant role in regional energy security.
China’s priorities are domestic, not regional
As the world’s largest oil importer, China has much in common with neighboring import-dependent countries weathering the Strait of Hormuz supply disruption. Yet it is largely absent from emerging regional policy discussions over new cooperative energy security planning mechanisms and institutions.
Over the past eight months, China has focused on domestic energy priorities—and its actions have sometimes harmed other Asian importers. Only a week after the US and Israeli attack on Iran, China banned export licenses for nearly all petroleum products. China relaxed those restrictions in subsequent months, but in October—after a significant decline in stocks of diesel and other fuels—Beijing again restricted product exports.
China is only the third largest petroleum product exporter in East Asia (after South Korea and Singapore), but unexpected changes to its export quotas alter market balances. For example, China supplied nearly one-third of Australia’s jet fuel imports in 2025, so its March jet fuel ban left Australian airlines scrambling for alternatives.
More broadly, China’s lack of transparency creates challenges for its neighbors. Its 2025-March 2026 inventory builds supported global oil demand, while a combination of lower refinery runs, caps on domestic fuel prices, and export restrictions contributed to an unprecedented decline in crude imports between February and June. Analysts note that China’s pricing power in oil markets stems from the timing and volume of its crude purchases. But while domestic considerations drive these decisions, they often leave China’s neighbors to plan around its actions. Despite the announcement of an ASEAN-China Energy Cooperation Partnership, its neighbors have reason to be cautious about China’s commitment.
After steep declines in the early months of the energy shock, Asian oil imports have rebounded. But the disruption has affected all importers that depend on Middle Eastern oil and gas. Japan typically imports more than 90 percent of its crude oil from the Middle East, so it has been forced to find alternatives from the United States or Latin America (in September, US crude oil accounted for 27 percent of Japan’s imports, up from 3 percent the previous year). India, which normally imports most of its liquefied petroleum gas from the Middle East, has turned to the United States for supply. Other Asian importers have struggled to secure petrochemicals feedstocks.
Importers are re-evaluating their supplier relationships. As International Energy Agency (IEA) Executive Director Fatih Birol stated at an April 2026 Atlantic Council event, importers now have three important objectives: “Diversify from whom you get your energy. Diversify your energy mix. And diversify your trade routes.” This is a difficult task for Asian importers with longstanding dependence on the Middle East, especially those with refineries configured to process crude oil grades from the Gulf and Iraq.
Addressing energy security threats with new institutions
Governments in the region see two major threats to their energy security. First, the shale revolution and the decline in US oil imports have given Washington freer rein to act in ways that can raise their energy costs and jeopardize supplies. And second, that global energy security institutions are no longer fit for purpose, since they were created amid the 1970s oil shocks—when Asia made up a much smaller share of the global economy and global oil and gas consumption.
Energy leaders see a need for new Asian energy security architecture, as governments seek to diversify supplies, build inventories, and explore joint purchasing and sharing mechanisms. Japan aims to lead this effort and has proposed several new programs to bolster energy security.
In Manila last week, leaders from Japan and Southeast Asia updated plans for the Tokyo-led Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) initiative and the related Partnership on Wide Energy and Resource Resilience Asia (POWERR Asia) framework. The AZEC action plan emphasizes cooperation on emissions reductions, carbon removal, and decarbonization of the transportation sector. Takaichi also proposed a new Asian oil security task force and referred to it as “an Asian version of the International Energy Agency.”
In April, Japan committed up to 1.5 trillion yen ($9.4 billion) under POWERR Asia to support regional procurement of new hydrocarbon supplies, infrastructure to bolster fuel storage and supply chain resilience in Asia, and diversification of energy sources. State institutions including the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC) and Japan Bank for International Cooperation are expected to support these plans that aim to broadly support Asian energy security. In several bills expected to be approved by Japan’s Diet in December, Takaichi’s government tasks JOGMEC with investing in alternative supply infrastructure including bypass pipelines and storage facilities.
At the Japan-ASEAN summit in Manila, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also proposed a new “POWERR Gulf” initiative to enhance cooperation between oil exporters in the Gulf and Asian importers. Inventories will likely be a key focus. Japan in particular is already building on existing joint stockpiling with Gulf national oil companies Saudi Aramco, Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, and Kuwait Petroleum Corporation. On November 20, Saudi Arabia and Japan announced an expanded joint oil stockpiling program. Japan intends to buy 8 million barrels of Saudi crude oil to replenish its stockpiles, and will lend Saudi Arabia new crude oil storage capacity of 16 million barrels, in addition to Aramco’s current 8.2 million barrels of capacity. Under Japan’s current joint oil stockpiling program, Gulf national oil companies lease storage capacity and use it for commercial operations in normal times, but Japanese companies have preferential rights to this crude oil in times of emergency. If the broader region embraces POWERR Gulf, the Gulf-Japan arrangement could become a template for other nations.
Asia will need more than one energy blueprint
The effectiveness of these new energy security initiatives remains to be seen. Japan and other countries in the region will remain highly dependent on the Middle East for crude oil and petroleum products. Energy resource endowments and energy systems also vary greatly across ASEAN countries, so their vulnerabilities and planning principles may differ from one country to the next.
Governments also face a strategic choice. After the second oil and gas price shock in five years, some policymakers in Southeast Asia and South Asia may lean toward more drastic changes in energy policy to emphasize resilience and use of domestic energy resources. Governments in these regions may well decide to direct scarce resources toward expanding electrification, renewable energy generation, battery storage, and grid resilience rather than new fossil fuel infrastructure.
It is notable that Japan is playing such a prominent role in region-wide energy security initiatives. This is unsurprising, since import-dependent Japan excels in long-term energy security planning and policy, including through its Strategic Energy Plans. Some officials and analysts in the broader region, however, worry that the proposed frameworks are too focused on fossil fuels, arguing that new investment should focus on electrification and renewable energy.
Opportunities for energy security leadership
As Asian governments devise new plans and institutions to bolster energy security and resilience, China is both absent and inescapable. China is the world’s largest oil importer, holds the world’s largest oil stockpiles, and is a key customer for nearly all the Gulf countries. More than any other importer, its actions will affect prices and energy security for its neighbors.
Beyond the oil and gas sector, China’s “electrostate” model and its many innovations in electrification, electric vehicle manufacturing, battery technology, and clean energy deployment will be important for Asian countries seeking to cut import dependence and build energy resilience. Yet it is not playing an especially active role in emerging multilateral discussions about how to bolster energy security in Asia. China’s lack of transparency and focus on domestic issues leaves a policy and planning gap that Japan is well positioned to fill.

title: Tentara Nasional Indonesia Angkatan Laut, U.S. Navy commence CARAT Indonesia 2026
zh_title: 印度尼西亚国家陆军海军和美国海军启动 CARAT Indonesia 2026
summary: 2026 年 11 月 25 日，印度尼西亚泗水（2026 年 11 月 25 日）——来自美国第七舰队和印度尼西亚国家海军部队 (TNI-AL) 的海防部队于 11 月 25 日在泗水举行会议，开始印度尼西亚海上合作准备和训练 (CARAT)。第 32 届 CARAT 印度尼西亚演习以开幕式启动，以美国和印度尼西亚之间之前的海上演习和行动为基础。 CARAT是一项海上演习，旨在促进地区安全合作，维护和加强海上伙伴关系，增强参演部队之间的互操作性
content:
2026 年 11 月 25 日

印度尼西亚泗水（2026 年 11 月 25 日）——来自美国第七舰队和印度尼西亚国家海军部队 (TNI-AL) 的海防部队于 11 月 25 日在泗水召开会议，开始印度尼西亚海上合作准备和训练 (CARAT)。

第 32 届 CARAT 印度尼西亚演习以开幕式启动，以美国和印度尼西亚之间之前的海上演习和行动为基础。 CARAT是一项海上演习，旨在促进地区安全合作，维护和加强海上伙伴关系，增强参演部队之间的互操作性。

美国驻泗水总领事克里斯·格林表示：“CARAT 代表了美国和印度尼西亚共同致力于促进整个印度-太平洋地区的海上安全和战备。” “30 多年来，CARAT 不断增强我们在广泛的海军能力领域并肩工作的能力。”
第 77 特遣部队 (CTF) 指挥官的复仇者级反水雷舰 USS Warrior (MCM 10) 于 11 月 25 日抵达印度尼西亚，启动初步活动。演习的海上阶段还将有来自 CTF-72 的一架 P-8A 海神海上巡逻和侦察机、三艘 TNI-AL 西格玛级护卫舰、法尼级反水雷舰 KRI Pulau Fani (MCMV 731) 和 KRI Pulau Fanildo (MCMV 732)、两架空客 AS656 Panther 直升机和一架 TNI-AL CN 235 飞机。 TNI-AL。此次迭代的海上阶段将以反潜战演习、水雷对抗最佳实践以及水面行动小组协调来进行跨部队指挥和控制为特色。

支持 CARAT 印度尼西亚 2026 的其他人员和工作人员包括美国第七舰队中队第 7 驱逐舰中队 (DESRON) 的指挥官，以及来自 CTF-73、CTF-75 和太平洋海军信息战中心的主题专家。主题专家交流 (SMEE) 主题将包括航空、网络、打捞潜水、爆炸物处理和 **U.S.-TNI-AL** 联合音乐表演。在泗水岸上举行的 SMEE 将通过建立人与人之间的关系来促进信息共享并促进海上互操作性。
“我们感谢印度尼西亚合作伙伴在泗水的热情欢迎和热情款待，”CTF-76 参谋长兼代表团团长美国海军上尉阿方扎·怀特 (Alfonza White) 说。 “CARAT 加强了我们的协调，建立了互信，并帮助我们维护了一个自由开放的印太地区。”

CARAT是一项长期演习系列，旨在增强美国及其伙伴部队共同行动应对该地区共同海上挑战的能力。

作为美国海军在东南亚前沿部署的DESRON，DESRON-7担任东南亚作战地区指定舰艇的主要战术和作战指挥官。

美国第七舰队是海军最大的前沿部署编号舰队，经常与盟友和伙伴互动和行动，以维护自由开放的印度太平洋地区。

【原文 English Original】
25 November 2026

SURABAYA, Indonesia (Nov. 25, 2026) — Maritime defense forces from U.S. 7th Fleet and Tentara Nasional Indonesia Angkatan Laut (TNI-AL) convened in Surabaya, Nov. 25, to commence Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) Indonesia.

The 32nd iteration of CARAT Indonesia launched with an opening ceremony, building upon previous maritime exercises and operations between the U.S. and Indonesia. CARAT is a maritime exercise designed to promote regional security cooperation, maintain and strengthen maritime partnerships, and enhance interoperability among participating forces.

“CARAT represents a commitment shared by the United States and Indonesia to promote maritime security and readiness across the Indo-Pacific,” said Chris Green, U.S. Consul General in Surabaya. “After more than 30 years, CARAT continues to enhance our ability to work side-by-side across a wide range of naval competencies.”

Avenger-class mine countermeasures ship USS Warrior (MCM 10) from Commander, Task Force (CTF) 77 arrived in Indonesia, Nov. 25, to kick off preliminary events. The sea-phase of the exercise will also feature a P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft from CTF-72, as well as three TNI-AL Sigma-class corvettes, Fani-class mine countermeasures vessels KRI Pulau Fani (MCMV 731) and KRI Pulau Fanildo (MCMV 732), two Airbus AS656 Panther helicopters, and one TNI-AL CN 235 aircraft from TNI-AL. The sea-phase of this iteration will feature anti-submarine warfare drills, mine countermeasures best practices, and surface action group coordination to exercise command and control across units.

Additional personnel and staff supporting CARAT Indonesia 2026 include Commander, Destroyer Squadron (DESRON) 7, the U.S. 7th Fleet Band, and subject matter experts from CTF-73, CTF-75, and Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific. Subject matter expert exchange (SMEE) topics will include aviation, cyber, salvage diving, explosive ordnance disposal, and **U.S.–TNI-AL** combined musical performances. The SMEEs, held ashore in Surabaya, will facilitate information-sharing and promote interoperability at sea through building people-to-people relationships.

“We are grateful to our Indonesian partners for their warm welcome and hospitality in Surabaya,” said U.S. Navy Capt. Alfonza White, chief of staff, CTF-76, and head of delegation. “CARAT strengthens our coordination, builds mutual trust, and helps us preserve a free and open Indo-Pacific.”

CARAT is a long-standing exercise series designed to enhance U.S. and partner forces abilities to operate together in response to shared maritime challenges in the region.

As the U.S. Navy’s forward-deployed DESRON in Southeast Asia, DESRON-7 serves as the primary tactical and operational commander of assigned ships in the Southeast Asia area of operations.

U.S. 7th Fleet, the Navy’s largest forward-deployed numbered fleet, routinely interacts and operates with allies and partners in preserving a free and open Indo-Pacific.

summary: 美国海军和日本海上自卫队 (JMSDF) 于 2026 年 11 月 10 日至 26 日在日本细岛附近举行了 2026 年水雷战演习 3JA (MINEX 3JA)。MINEX 3JA 是美国海军和日本海上自卫队每年举行的一系列演习的一部分，旨在提高水雷对抗行动的熟练程度并加强协调。此次演习以之前的 JA 系列迭代为基础，其中包括 2026 年 7 月 9 日至 24 日举行的 MINEX 2JA。在为期 16 天的双边演习中，参与者共同努力清除模拟雷区，锻炼了部队级别的机敏能力

美国海军和日本海上自卫队 (JMSDF) 于 2026 年 11 月 10 日至 26 日在日本细岛附近进行了 2026 年第 3JA 次水雷战演习 (MINEX 3JA)。

MINEX 3JA 是美国海军和日本海上自卫队每年举行的一系列演习的一部分，旨在提高水雷对抗行动的熟练程度并加强协调。此次演习以之前的 JA 系列迭代为基础，包括 2026 年 7 月 9 日至 24 日举行的 MINEX 2JA。在为期 16 天的双边演习中，参与者共同努力清除模拟雷区，演练扫雷、探测和压制等单位级战术。

第 77 特遣部队 (CTF) 指挥官、美国海军上校戈登·斯科特·威尔斯 (Gorden Scott Wells) 表示：“能够与我们的日本合作伙伴一起工作，并继续发展我们在水雷对抗领域的强大关系，始终是一种荣幸。几十年来，我们一直在与日本海上自卫队一起开展 JA 系列行动，并且我们仍然致力于提高我们在这一关键作战能力方面的集体能力。”

日本海上自卫队水雷战部队、CTF-75 和 CTF-77 指挥官齐心协力，指挥协调一致的扫雷、扫雷和消除地雷任务。这次训练使所有参与单位能够完善通信协议和战术程序，同时最大限度地提高集体海上能力。
参演的美国海军部队包括复仇者级水雷对抗舰USS Chief (MCM 14)、爆炸物处理(EOD)机动部队5的人员以及分配给第7水雷对抗大队的人员。日本海上自卫队参与者包括浦贺级扫雷舰母舰 JS Uraga (MST-463)；淡路级海洋扫雷舰 JS Awaji (MSO-304)；平岛级海岸扫雷舰 JS Hatsushima (MSC-606)；菅岛级沿海扫雷舰 JS Izushima (MSC-687)、JS Aishima (MSC-688)、JS Aoshima (MSC-689)、JS Miyajima (MSC-690) 和 JS Kuroshima (MSC-692)；和潜水补给船YDT-02。空中和作战支援由日本海上自卫队川崎 P-1 和 P-3C 海上巡逻机、反水雷直升机 (MCH-101) 以及多支日本海上自卫队排爆部队提供。

CTF-77指挥反水雷资产清除水雷，以确保海上贸易的自由流通以及美国、盟国和伙伴国船只在和平时期和冲突期间的行动自由。

此次演习在美国第七舰队作战区内进行。美国第七舰队是海军最大的前沿部署编号舰队，经常与盟友和伙伴互动和行动，维护自由开放的印度太平洋地区。

【原文 English Original】
The U.S. Navy and Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF) conducted Mine Warfare Exercise 3JA (MINEX 3JA) 2026 in the vicinity of Hososhima, Japan, Nov. 10–26, 2026.

MINEX 3JA is part of an annual series of exercises held between the U.S. Navy and JMSDF designed to increase proficiency and strengthen coordination in mine countermeasure operations. This exercise builds on previous iterations of the JA series, including MINEX 2JA, which took place from July 9 – 24, 2026. During the 16-day bilateral exercise, participants worked together to clear simulated minefields, exercising unit-level tactics such as mine hunting, detection, and neutralization.

“It is always an honor and a privilege to work alongside our Japanese partners and continue to build on our powerful relationship within the mine countermeasures community,” said U.S. Navy Capt. Gorden Scott Wells, Commander, Task Force (CTF) 77. “We have been conducting the JA series with the JMSDF for decades, and we remain dedicated to advancing our collective capacity in this critical operational capability.”

Working in unison, JMSDF Mine Warfare Force, CTF-75, and CTF-77 commanders directed coordinated mine hunting, mine sweeping, and mine neutralization tasks. This training allowed all participating units to refine communication protocols and tactical procedures while maximizing their collective maritime capability.

Avenger-class mine countermeasures ship USS Chief (MCM 14), personnel from Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Mobile Unit 5, and staff assigned to Mine Countermeasures Group 7 comprised the participating U.S. Navy units. JMSDF participants included Uraga-class minesweeper tender JS Uraga (MST-463); Awaji-class ocean minesweeper JS Awaji (MSO-304); Hirashima-class coastal minesweeper JS Hatsushima (MSC-606); Sugashima-class coastal minesweepers JS Izushima (MSC-687), JS Aishima (MSC-688), JS Aoshima (MSC-689), JS Miyajima (MSC-690), and JS Kuroshima (MSC-692); and diving tender YDT-02. Aerial and operational support was provided by JMSDF Kawasaki P-1 and P-3C maritime patrol aircraft, mine countermeasures helicopters (MCH-101), and multiple embarked JMSDF EOD units.

CTF-77 directs mine countermeasures assets in the clearance of sea mines to ensure the free flow of commerce by sea and the freedom of movement for U.S., allied, and partner nation vessels during peacetime and in conflict.

The exercise took place within the U.S. 7th Fleet area of operations. U.S. 7th Fleet, the Navy's largest forward-deployed numbered fleet, routinely interacts and operates with allies and partners in preserving a free and open Indo-Pacific.

**NEWS** | Nov. 25, 2026

# Tentara Nasional Indonesia Angkatan Laut, U.S. Navy commence CARAT Indonesia 2026

By Lt. Camillia Nguyen, Commander, Destroyer Squadron 7 Public Affairs

 SURABAYA, Indonesia–
Maritime defense forces from U.S. 7th Fleet and Tentara Nasional Indonesia Angkatan Laut (TNI-AL) convened in Surabaya, Nov. 25, to commence Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT) Indonesia.

The 32nd iteration of CARAT Indonesia launched with an opening ceremony, building upon previous maritime exercises and operations between the U.S. and Indonesia. CARAT is a maritime exercise designed to promote regional security cooperation, maintain and strengthen maritime partnerships, and enhance interoperability among participating forces.

“CARAT represents a commitment shared by the United States and Indonesia to promote maritime security and readiness across the Indo-Pacific,” said Chris Green, U.S. Consul General in Surabaya. “After more than 30 years, CARAT continues to enhance our ability to work side-by-side across a wide range of naval competencies.”

Avenger-class mine countermeasures ship USS Warrior (MCM 10) from Commander, Task Force (CTF) 77 arrived in Indonesia, Nov. 25, to kick off preliminary events. The sea-phase of the exercise will also feature a P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol and reconnaissance aircraft from CTF-72, as well as three TNI-AL Sigma-class corvettes, Fani-class mine countermeasures vessels KRI Pulau Fani (MCMV 731) and KRI Pulau Fanildo (MCMV 732), two Airbus AS656 Panther helicopters, and one TNI-AL CN 235 aircraft from TNI-AL. The sea-phase of this iteration will feature anti-submarine warfare drills, mine countermeasures best practices, and surface action group coordination to exercise command and control across units.

Additional personnel and staff supporting CARAT Indonesia 2026 include Commander, Destroyer Squadron (DESRON) 7, the U.S. 7th Fleet Band, and subject matter experts from CTF-73, CTF-75, and Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific. Subject matter expert exchange (SMEE) topics will include aviation, cyber, salvage diving, explosive ordnance disposal, and **U.S.–TNI-AL** combined musical performances. The SMEEs, held ashore in Surabaya, will facilitate information-sharing and promote interoperability at sea through building people-to-people relationships.

“We are grateful to our Indonesian partners for their warm welcome and hospitality in Surabaya,” said U.S. Navy Capt. Alfonza White, chief of staff, CTF-76, and head of delegation. “CARAT strengthens our coordination, builds mutual trust, and helps us preserve a free and open Indo-Pacific.”

CARAT is a long-standing exercise series designed to enhance U.S. and partner forces abilities to operate together in response to shared maritime challenges in the region.

As the U.S. Navy’s forward-deployed DESRON in Southeast Asia, DESRON-7 serves as the primary tactical and operational commander of assigned ships in the Southeast Asia area of operations.

U.S. 7th Fleet, the Navy’s largest forward-deployed numbered fleet, routinely interacts and operates with allies and partners in preserving a free and open Indo-Pacific.

Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

content:
Fundraiser by David Xia : Fighting for legal fairness
David Xia and 2 others are organizing this fundraiser.
Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)
Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.
Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.
Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.
Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.
Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.
Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.
Please contact Julia Lee and other volunteers through [email redacted] for the details.
We’re most grateful to your attention, encouragement, support and great help!
原北大教授、政治异议人士，现时政/财经新闻评论人夏业良先生（美国之音/自由亚洲电台/博讯/新唐人等媒体）因网络质疑和评论，而被中国逃亡商人郭文贵花钱组织围攻/抹黑，并在美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦法院提交所谓诽谤指控和滥诉。
夏先生通过电视节目和推特对郭的所谓爆料（包括最高机密信息）进行了质疑和批评，郭雇佣组织了对夏及其家人的网络围攻，同时指控夏对他进行诽谤并索赔五百万美元。
郭滥用美国司法资源， 目前正在进行中的诉讼超过41起，郭宣称他计划起诉至少91位对他进行诽谤的个人。
夏先生和其他被告均无力承担雇佣合格并有经验的律师之花费。因此在众多网络旁观者的建议下开始了募捐应对郭之诉讼的律师费用。
夏先生将把募捐得款只用于本案诉讼之中，并且得到若干志愿者的支持和帮助，他们协助收集募捐款项/记账与募捐监督等工作。本次募捐活动的目标已设定为十万美元，并且已经开设了一个名为“GoFundMe”之软件的募捐账户平台以作为主要募捐渠道。
请各位捐助者通过电子邮箱：[email redacted] 与Julia Lee等志愿者联系，以获得相关细节。

summary: Fundraiser by Heather Liu : Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case Heather Liu is organizing this fundraiser. What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex
content:
Fundraiser by Heather Liu : Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case
Heather Liu is organizing this fundraiser.
What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex forced on me, followed by lies and denial. Then, rare moments of hope, followed by setbacks tinged with revenge from a father whose fear of revealing truth drives him to deny his child’s existence. This child is my daughter. For 20 years I’ve hidden the nightmare involving her origin by my silence, partly due to the sense of shame and partly because the father of my child is a influential public figure. Till the rapist has pushed us to a corner by threatening our existence with vicious conspiracy theories.
（我經歷了任何一位女性都不該經歷的事情。先是遭遇性侵，接著還要面對謊言、抵賴和詆毀。過去20年來，間或閃現的希望，卻因我女兒的生父拒絕承認這孩子的存在，而淹沒在長久的幻滅中。過去20年來，我一直對女兒的身世三緘其口，讓一段揮之不去的夢魘深藏內心，一方面出於羞辱感，另一方面無法面對孩子的生父作為一個公眾人物給我心靈帶來的扭曲。）
With your help, the truth of our experience will be told. When it is, I hope justice will prevail. This is why I’m emerging from the shadows.
（因您伸出援手，我將得以說出這段真實的經歷。當真相大白的那一天到來，我希望正義能夠隨之彰顯。）
In 2000, I was a journalist working for a local Chinese newspaper in Los Angeles. I was assigned to interview a famous Chinese dissident, a political refugee in America, who people called the “Godfather of the Democratic Movement in China.” I wrote the story, but in doing so, my life was changed forever by his sexual assault of me.
（2000年，身為洛杉磯當地一家中文媒體記者的我，被派去採訪一位著名的中國異議人士，也是我本人非常敬仰的政治流亡者、一位被視為「中國民主運動之父」的風雲人物。我完成了採訪任務，然而我的個人生活卻因今生與他這唯一的遭逢而徹底脫軌。）
Let’s just say, nine months after I did that story, I gave birth to my daughter, who bore no resemblance to my then-husband. My husband knew why since I’d told him about the sexual assault after it happened. My marriage ended, and my life as a single mom began. To protect my daughter and me from possible backlash about how she was conceived and her father’s identity, I kept my ordeal quiet. The two of us moved to Hong Kong.
（在我做了那次採訪的9個月之後，我的女兒降生了。她跟我當時的丈夫長得一點也不像，而我丈夫也並不感到驚訝，因為我早跟他坦白了我遭遇性侵的事。我的婚姻其實從那時起已名存實亡，我作為一個單親母親的生涯也即將開始。為了遠離各種因孩子身世而產生的猜忌，讓我和孩子可以過安靜而屬於自己的生活，同時也為了可以就近得到父母家人的幫忙照顧，我帶著孩子離開了美國，赴香港尋找發展機會。）
Through the years I never thought about contacting my daughter's biological father, whom I met only once. I didn’t consider doing this even after I lost my job as an editor in 2012. But then a former colleague, Beifeng, left Hong Kong for the United States. He’d criticized me for "depriving the child the right to be recognized by her father," and later persuaded me to let him bring a lock of my daughter’s hair, wrapped it in tissue paper, that he took with him to the United States.
（多年來，我從未想過要聯絡孩子的生父，那個我只見過一面的人，哪怕是2012年我失業的時候也沒萌生這個打算。我根本已經忘記了這個人，要不是當時正要動身赴美的前同事北風（我告訴了他我的孩子生父是誰，但沒有讓他知道詳情，他也沒有探問）批評我「剝奪孩子認父的權利」。他太太當即揪了孩子幾根頭髮，用手紙包了起來。）
Months later, my heart sank when Beifeng reported back to me that this man had denied everything, even the possibility of knowing me, let alone the possibility of having fathered a child. He’d committed this horrible crime against me, but he refused to acknowledge this truth. For to accept that he’d fathered a daughter, he’d have to admit how she came to existence. It appeared that he was refusing to allow his carefully crafted story about his “heroic” life to be marred by acknowledging his daughter’s existence.
（幾個月之後，北風帶來消息並深表意外地說，孩子的生父得知自己可能有個孩子時的反應，竟是敷衍和閃躲，好像根本不可能有這回事一樣。他當然寧肯忘記自己做過的事，但真相怎麼能因你不想面對就可以不承認、孩子怎麼可以就這樣當她不存在呢？就像他後來在郵件裡提到的，他所關切的，是這事將來在他的回憶錄裡該怎麼寫，而不是他身為人父應該盡什麼責。他在意的只是他自己英雄般的人生，無論如何不能留下任何污點。）
After this news reached me, I was diagnosed with clinical depression and started to see a doctor regularly. Professionally, however, I had to appear calm and collected so I could earn a living that would support the two of us. I worked as a freelance writer and translator, while also raising my daughter on my own.
（我聞訊心裡沉了一下，不久開始意識恍惚，甚至試過下班下車記不起回家的方向。我遠在北京的母親聽說之後，在電話的另一頭啜泣得聲音哽咽。2013年2月，我被確診患上抑鬱症。失業更兼病倒，令我們母女的生計雪上加霜，這期間我成為自由撰稿人，還要硬撐著努力譯書維持生計。好在偶爾有父母幫手、妹妹接濟一下，才度過了一段危機。）
Five years later, in 2018, in the midst of #MeToo movement, when sexual abuse and harassment were receiving public attention globally, rumors spread online about this famous Chinese man having fathered an illegitimate child. At that point, I contacted him by phone from Hong Kong and boldly asked for child support.
（一晃又過了5年，時間到了2018年，在#MeToo（「我也是受害者」）運動的聲浪中，性侵和性騷擾現象的普遍存在引起了全球性輿論關注。在此期間，網上首次出現了對我女兒的生父「不認親」的議論。已變得反應遲緩的我這才開始應對，邁出了主動聯繫孩子生父這一步。）
He agreed to a DNA test that was performed privately in Washington D.C.., The DNA results proved that he was Charlotte's father. The person who shared the results with him said that he had responded positively to having a daughter. Accordingly, when I contacted him again, he promised to assist us by at least paying for her education. But later on, since I would not change my tone on the unhappy encounter with him in the past, he decided to deny being Charlotte’s father and began to challenge the DNA results, shirked his responsibility as her biological father, and ignored that I was a victim of his violent sexual assault.
（他於是主動提出做個DNA鑑定，並指定了一位背景相當可靠的前白宮幕僚做中間人，在華盛頓特區進行了DNA樣本的收集與鑑定。結果出來後，中間人率先通知我，說結果證明魏先生是孩子的生父無疑，並告訴我，魏先生對鑑定結果表示認可並顯得「很開心」。據此，在我與孩子的生父再次聯繫時，他表示自己起碼會負擔孩子的大學學費。但真到了時候他又變卦了，甚至仗著沒有把DNA鑑定結果如約給我們，便想將已經做過DNA鑑定這事也想賴掉。）
The rest of the story is detailed in Huaizhao Liu v. Jingsheng Wei, case #1:19-cv-03344, which was heard in the Washington, D.C. federal court. Charlotte’s father managed to find the funds necessary to hire a high-powered defense attorney to help him to deny both our dignity and his basic obligations of paternity.
（後來的事情見華盛頓特區聯邦法院卷宗（Case Number 1:19-cv-03344）。我女兒的生父大手筆聘請了專攻白領犯罪辯護的名牌大狀為自己的辯護律師，竭力搬弄法律條文進行技術性規避，想就此永遠掩蓋真相，踐踏我們母女的權益與尊嚴。）
We believe that Charlotte’s biological father should be forced to keep his promise of supporting her education, and we are asking that he release the DNA test results to us. His 19-year old daughter deserves to know the truth.
（我們堅信，法庭應該為這位竭力否認已經做過親子鑑定的生父驗明正身，然後強制他履行他的諾言，承擔他女兒的學費。我們堅信，他19歲的女兒有權利知曉真相。）
The weight of evidence is on our side, but we risk losing the lawsuit that we are filing against him if we cannot raise the money we need to hire an attorney who is as capable as his lawyer. What is at risk is Charlotte's right to a quality education, along with the legally binding acknowledgement of his paternity.
（儘管我們掌握活生生的證據，但如果籌不到聘請律師的費用，單憑我們自訴，將無法應對複雜的陪審團庭審程序。立案至今一年多來，被告採取躲和拖的戰術，先是躲傳票，然後提出「司法管轄權」爭議逼我們撤案，一計不成又援引「多國籍」條款，將案子從特區高等法院轉移到聯邦法院。）
With your assistance – with your contributions – we intend to hire an attorney who is experienced in sexual assault and paternity cases. We hope to win this #MeToo case and pursue respectful, equal and democratic human relationship in Chinese community.
（您的捐助將幫助我們聘請到專攻性侵案和親子案官司的律師，幫我們贏得這場事關尊嚴、平等、人權以及人性的人身傷害官司，並藉此推動美國的華人社區乃至全球華人的觀念進步與行為的現代化。）
Here are some online stories and commentary about this, in Chinese:
https://www.storm.mg/article/2891777?mode=whole
(by Liao Yiwu, award winner of Human Rights Watch Hellman-Hammett Grant 2003, the German Geschwister-Scholl-Preis 2011 and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade 2012.)
（作者/廖亦武，詩人、流亡作家與底層歷史記錄者。2012年德國書業和平獎得主，並曾獲美國《當代基督教》雜誌頒發的「最佳圖書奬」、德國書業協會頒發的「紹爾兄妹獎」、德國廣播協會頒發的「最佳廣播劇奬」及德國阿夏芬堡頒發的「公民勇氣奬」。2013年，法國政府頒發給廖亦武「法蘭西文學藝術軍官獎章」。2018年，廖亦武獲美國紐約瓦茨拉夫 哈維爾圖書基金會頒發「無懼危難作家獎」。）
http://minzhuzhongguo.org/MainArtShow.aspx?AID=105641
(by Qi JIazhen, writer in exile, author of autobiographical series: Tears of the Goddess of Liberty and Red Dog. Qi is the Chairwoman of the Women Writers committee, Independent Chinese PEN Center.)
（作者/齊家貞，流亡作家，著有系列傳記《自由神的眼泪──父女两代囚徒的真實故事》（後改名《黑牆裡的倖存者》和《紅狗：—個被釋女囚的真實故事》在香港和台灣出版。齊家貞曾先後擔任國際筆會獨立中文筆會理事會理事、副會長、秘書長等職務，並在澳洲建立了“齊氏文化基金會”，每年頒發“推動中國進步獎”截至2019年已連續頒獎12屆。）
https://liuvswei.blogspot.com/2020/08/metoo.html
(by Lau Kayee, Chairwoman of Network for Women In Politics, Hong Kong; Spokeswoman of Hong Kong Civil Human Rights Front.)
（作者/劉家儀，香港婦女參政網絡主席，六四新生代秘書長，支聯會常委，香港市民捍衛人權陣線發言人。）
With your contributions, we will be able to set a positive example for #MeToo victims by raising awareness about women’s and children's rights, globally.
因您的資助，我們將能夠為#MeToo運動傷害者們建立一個積極的個案，為提高女性及孩童的權利意識而有所貢獻。

Fundraiser by Kuber Poudel Chhetri : Needs for Human Right Activist
Kuber Poudel Chhetri is organizing this fundraiser.
Mr. Suk Bahadur Subba is a well known Human Rights Activist working for the politically persecuted people of the country of Bhutan. Bhutan is a country located between the boarders of India and China whose people have been persecuted for the past 25 years.
Mr. Subba is considered by the Royal Government of Bhutan to be a political dissident for fighting against the Racial Discrimination and Ethnic Cleasning of the Bhutanese People.
Mr. Subba is in desperate need of medical treatment for the transplant of both of his kidney's. We are reaching out to raise USD $ 45, 000.00 to send to India to help save the life of this man who has continually risked his own life to save the lives of hundreds of thousands of Bhutanese refugees.

content:
Fundraiser by Boston Standswithhk : US Hong Kong Safe Harbor Postcard Campaign
Boston Standswithhk is organizing this fundraiser.
***When donation, make as anonymous if you wish to hide the donator's name and make the TIPS to 0.00***
While US-China tensions continue to escalate and the November presidential elections loom near, as Hongkongers living in the United States (or any informed person in the world), we must not forget or turn a blind eye to the CCP’s continuous oppression on Hongkongers and other minority groups in China, such as Uyghurs, Tibetans, and Mongolians. With the promulgation of the new National Security Law on June 30, 2020, the government has since been arresting and charging dissidents with these vaguely-worded laws that may entail life imprisonment. In the past month alone, 12 Hong Kongers fleeing protest-related charges have been detained in China and denied meetings with lawyers since August 23, 2020; Legislative Council elections had been postponed a year in the name of “public health concerns” amidst a mass arrest of candidates; media mogul Jimmy Lai, who runs the only pro-democratic print newspaper in Hong Kong, has been arrested with the National Security Law; and the Education Bureau has begun actively censoring content they deemed politically incorrect in Liberal Studies textbooks, including concepts like “civil disobedience” and “separation of powers”, and images of Lennon Walls. Up until today, the administration has arrested more than 10,000 Hong Kongers, charged over 2,200, deployed water cannons, fired more than 16,000 tear gas canisters and over 10,000 rubber bullets against its own people. Freedom of speech, freedom of assembly and political rights as we knew it have been thoroughly eroded.
11月的美國總統大選逐漸逼近，中美關係日漸緊張，作為居住在美國的香港人或是在這個世界上任何有良知的人，面對中共對香港、維吾爾族、藏族和蒙古族的持續壓逼，我們不能容忍，更不能視而不見。自2020年6月30日頒布《國家安全法》以來，政府持續逮捕異見人​​士，並以措辭含糊的法律起訴抗爭者，香港的司法制度已經徹底淪為政府的打壓工具。及後更有12名香港抗爭者為了逃離這種不公義的審判欲流亡台灣，卻被中共非法拘捕。他們無法與律師會面，音訊全無。而香港人僅有的發聲方法——立法會選舉，卻因為「公共衛生風險」而被推遲一年；同時間，大批候選人被逮捕或是被拒絕參選。作為香港唯一異見紙媒《蘋果日報》的老闆黎智英被警方高調逮捕，《蘋果日報》總部更被大肆搜查。教育局亦積極審查通識科教科書中所謂的「政治不正確」內容，例如「公民抗命」和「三權分立」的概念，以及連儂牆相片。到今天為止，已經有超過10,000多名香港人被捕、2,200多人被起訴，警方向市民發射了超過16,000枚催淚彈和10,000多發橡皮子彈，令香港人長期生活在恐懼中。香港人的言論自由、集會自由和政治權利已被徹底侵蝕。
In light of the deteriorating situation, we plan to kickstart a new round of postcard campaign urging Congress to pass two bills related to Hong Kong as soon as possible - Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act (H.R.7415/S.4110), and Hong Kong People’s Freedom and Choice Act (H.R.7428/S.4229):
鑑於情況日益惡化，我們希望透過郵寄明信片給國會議員的方式，呼籲他們盡快通過兩項與香港有關的法案 —— 香港安全港法案 (H.R.7415 / S.4110) 和香港人民自由與選擇法(H.R.7428 / S.4229):
The Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act will designate certain Hong Kong residents who are victims of persecution or who have a well-founded fear of future persecution because of their peaceful political activities as Priority 2 refugees (excluded from refugee cap), allowing them and their spouses, children, parents to apply to the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program for protection. (Click here for more details)
《香港安全港法案》將指定某些遭受迫害，或因其參與和平的政治活動而感到恐懼的香港居民列為「優先級別2」的難民，且不受每年限額限制，亦允許他們及其配偶、子女、父母向「美國難民接納計劃」申請庇護。(詳情請瀏覽)
The Hong Kong People's Freedom and Choice Act will provide Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Hong Kongers, maintain Hong Kong’s status as autonomous for the purposes of immigration, provide special and expedited status for certain high-skilled Hong Kongers as well as expedite Permanent Resident status for Hong Kongers residing in the US. (Click here for more details)
《香港人民自由與選擇法》會為香港人提供臨時保護身份（TPS），維持香港在移民方面的自治地位，亦為部分香港專業人仕提供特殊和快速的身份，並加快辦理香港人的美國永久居民(綠卡)身份的程序。(詳情請瀏覽)
In our last postcard campaign pushing for the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act, we delivered over 3000 postcards to Congress. We aren’t part of any formal organization and do not have operation funds. We desperately call for your contribution again to help us deliver these postcards to Congress, to remind them of Hong Kong’s urgent situation and urge them to take immediate action. Your contribution would support our printing and delivery costs. Thank you so much!
在上一次推動《香港人權與民主法》的明信片運動中，我們向國會送出了超過3000張的明信片。我們不是任何正式組織的成員，也沒有運營資金，所以我們竭誠呼籲您為我們提供資金，並幫助我們將這些明信片送交您們所屬的國會議員，提醒他們香港的緊急狀況，並呼籲他們立即採取行動。所有受到的捐款將支持我們的打印和交付成本。萬分感謝！

content:
Fundraiser by Alan Wan : Help Alan Navigate Life in Political Exile
Alan’s fund provides groceries and rent for a political dissident facing exile abroad
Inspire others and help Alan build momentum.
Inspire others and help Alan build momentum.
Alan Wan is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Alan, and I am writing this with a sincere and humble heart.
I am a Chinese political dissident living in Houston, Texas. Because of my beliefs and my willingness to speak openly about freedom, human rights, and justice, I have faced serious threats and intimidation from the Chinese government. These pressures have made it impossible for me to safely return to China, where my family still lives. Every day, I carry the pain of being separated from my loved ones, uncertain when—or if—I will ever be able to reunite with them again.
Beyond the emotional suffering, I am now facing severe financial hardship. Due to restrictions and complications surrounding the transfer of my personal funds from abroad, I have been unable to access resources that I once depended on for survival. My savings are rapidly disappearing, and I am now struggling simply to cover basic daily necessities such as food, housing, transportation, and medical care.
This situation has left me feeling isolated and vulnerable. I never imagined that standing by my principles would lead to such profound personal sacrifice, but I continue to hold onto hope.
Today, I am reaching out with deep humility to ask for your support. Any assistance—whether financial help, practical resources, or connections to organizations that aid individuals in political exile—would mean more than words can express. Your kindness could help me maintain stability during this incredibly difficult chapter of my life and allow me to continue moving forward with dignity.
I am not asking for luxury, only for the chance to live safely and meet my most basic needs while I navigate these extraordinary challenges.
Thank you for taking the time to read my story. Your compassion, understanding, and support would be a lifeline during one of the hardest periods of my life.
Grocery and part of my rent.

content:
Fundraiser by Pie Formosa : Support Pie Formosa’s Independent Work
Inspire others and help Pie build momentum.
Inspire others and help Pie build momentum.
Pie Formosa is organizing this fundraiser.
I sometimes describe myself as a refugee from WeChat to Instagram — but I am also, quite literally, a refugee from China.
I am a political dissident, human rights activist, non-binary person and independent writer living with invisible disabilities, now continuing my work in Europe.
I write and create public work about censorship, authoritarianism, political memory, democracy, queer and trans freedom, refugee experiences, neurodiversity, and the cultural spaces where resistance survives.
For years, WeChat was one of the places where I published my work. Readers could easily support independent creators with small tips. Then the Chinese Communist Party shut down my account. I lost not only a platform, but also an audience, an archive, and a simple way for people to support my work.
This fundraiser is part of rebuilding that independence.
Living with invisible disabilities also means that conventional employment structures and constant high-intensity workloads are not always accessible or sustainable for me. I need a modest and stable income to make independent research, writing and human-rights work sustainable.
* research, writing and documentation
* travel to human-rights, democracy and civil-society events
* basic living costs that allow me to continue this work independently
If something I have written, documented or created has informed, helped or inspired you, even €1, €5 or €10 helps me keep this work alive. If donating is not possible, sharing this fundraiser also makes a real difference.
Authoritarianism depends on silence and forgetting. Independent voices survive because people choose to keep them alive.
Thank you for supporting my work.
https://linktr.ee/pieformosa

summary: Fundraiser by Mark Nygate : SAVE US FROM THE MEGA EMBASSY! SUPPORT OUR LEGAL CHALLENGE Mark Nygate is organizing this fundraiser. We are 100 families taking on the CCP - and we need your help. 我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」，由約一百戶職工家庭組成。我們懇請你伸出援手。 In 2018,
content:
Fundraiser by Mark Nygate : SAVE US FROM THE MEGA EMBASSY! SUPPORT OUR LEGAL CHALLENGE
Mark Nygate is organizing this fundraiser.
We are 100 families taking on the CCP - and we need your help.
我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」，由約一百戶職工家庭組成。我們懇請你伸出援手。
In 2018, our homes-key-worker flats in Tower Hamlets were sold in a secretive deal to the People's Republic of China. We had no say. No warning. And now, we face living under the shadow of a hostile superpower.
2018年，我們居住的Tower Hamlets地段，在未經通知、無任何諮詢下，被秘密售予中國政府。我們無從置喙，如今更面對一個敵對政權的威脅。
The UK Government is expected to approve plans to build the largest embassy in Europe - right here, at Royal Mint Court, next to the Tower of London… and directly on top of our homes.
英國政府即將批准於倫敦塔旁的皇家鑄幣廠（Royal Mint Court）興建歐洲最大規模的中國大使館，預定地點正正位於我們所居之上。
This is not just a planning dispute.
我們擔憂的不僅是一項城市規劃決策，而是一場關乎國家安全、人身安全與基本權利的危機。
China has never shown any regard for our safety - and now the Government and the Metropolitan Police have abandoned us too.
自2018年起，中國政府從未就此提供明確回應，我們甚至不知道會否被驅逐、是否仍能繼續安居於此。而如今，政府與執法機關也對我們置之不理。
We are the Royal Mint Court Residents Association. People backed our previous Crowdfunder campaign that helped pay for a barrister to present our evidence including an independent security assessment showing the serious risks to us from a terror attack on the mega-embassy.
我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」。我們之前的眾籌活動獲得許多人的支持，資助我們聘請資深大律師提交證據，包括一份獨立的安全評估報告，指出超級大使館可能帶來的恐襲風險。
We are now launching an urgent legal challenge - a Judicial Review - to change the law and stop this injustice.
我們現在正展開一項緊急法律挑戰 — 即司法覆核 — 希望改變現行法律，阻止這場不公。
We need your help to protect our community from the mighty Chinese Communist Party.
我們需要你的幫助，去保護我們的社區，免受強大的中國共產黨威脅。
Whatever you can spare us, will help David stand-up to Goliath.
We are seeking to pursue a Judicial Review because we have believed all along that the planning process has been flawed. Here are some of the reasons we think are likely to be relevant:
我們決定提起司法覆核，是因為我們始終認為整個規劃程序存在問題。以下是我們認為可能相關的一些原因：
“Closed mind”: Ministers may have signalled early approval to China, before formal procedures were followed, breaking the law and abusing planning powers. In a similar vein, objections disappeared after UK ministers returned from Beijing. Residents have felt like pawns in a geopolitical game since the start.
預設立場：部長們可能在正式程序開始前就向中方表示支持，違反法律並濫用規劃權力。在部長們從北京回來之後，原有的反對聲音突然消失。居民們從一開始就覺得自己成了地緣政治博弈中的棋子。
Security concerns: Building a fortified embassy with homes on site and critical infrastructure nearby, ignoring espionage concerns and the real human risk to dissidents, is indefensible.
安全隱患：在住宅區內及重要基礎設施附近建設高度防禦的大使館，無視間諜活動與對異見人士的人身威脅，完全不能接受。
Procedural unfairness: We were shut out of the process. No consultation. No transparency. No respect for the people who live here.
程序不公：我們被完全排除在決策過程之外。無諮詢、無透明、無對居民的尊重。
Legitimate expectation: We were promised due process and protection. We got silence.
合理期望落空：我們被承諾將獲程序保障與保護，實際卻是得不到任何保障。
We still live here. 100 families. Nurses, teachers, pensioners. Our 100 homes are on land now owned by the Chinese government. That means the Chinese ambassador is our landlord - with rights to enter our homes.
我們仍然住在這裡 ，足足一百戶家庭，包括護士、教師、退休人士。我們的一百個住所現已位於中國政府擁有的土地上。這代表中國大使成為我們的業主，有權進入我們的住所。
China refuses to answer us. Since 2018, we’ve begged for assurances: will we be evicted? Will we be safe? Can we stay? Beijing’s answer: not until we get planning permission. This refusal, and the proposal to install a temporary style wooden boundary fence as a dividing line, raises fears that the Chinese Government intends to take back the entire 100 apartments at St Mary Graces Court once they secure diplomatic status for the site, leaving us homeless.
中國拒絕回應我們的訴求。自2018年起，我們不斷尋求保證：我們會被驅逐嗎？我們是否安全？我們能否繼續居住？北京的答覆是：等規劃許可下來再說。這種拒絕，以及擬議中以臨時木欄分隔的做法，讓我們擔心中國政府一旦取得外交地位，將會收回整個St Mary Graces Court的100個單位，使我們流離失所。
This embassy is a fortress. It’s not a normal diplomatic building. It will have secret communications centres, fortified walls, and surveillance technology that can monitor our entire estate, even our bedrooms. It will also stand on top of critical UK cables that MI5 warn are a security risk to the UK.
這座大使館是一個堡壘，並非普通的外交建築。它將設有秘密通訊設施、加固圍牆、監控技術，可監視整個屋苑，甚至包括我們的睡房。而它的地基下方，更有英國重要電纜 ，MI5曾警告這是對國家安全的威脅。
The UK Government knows the risk - and ignored it. Our independent security report warns that this site puts families and national security at risk. Even the UK’s Head of Counter-Terrorism originally objected - citing threats to residents and dissidents. But since ministers returned from Beijing, objections have mysteriously vanished.
英國政府明知有風險，卻選擇無視。我們的獨立安全報告指出，該地點將危害居民與國家安全。甚至連英國反恐部門首長最初也曾反對 ， 指出對居民與異見人士的威脅。但自從部長從北京回來後，這些反對聲音神秘地消失。
Ministers made no mention of the 100 families living here. We are alarmed that the letters from Home Secretary Yvette Cooper and Foreign Secretary David Lammy have ignored the fact that UK families live in 100 apartments on the land that is actually part of Royal Mint court - and is owned by the Chinese government. Our Resident’s Chairman has personally appealed to ministers, submitted the full Crilly Consultants security report, and our plight has appeared in The Times, FT, BBC, CNN, and more. What is happening to democratic accountability in this country?
部長們從未提及這裡有一百戶居民。我們對內政大臣Yvette Cooper及外交大臣David Lammy的信件感到震驚，因為他們完全忽略了皇家鑄幣廠的土地上住有英國公民、100個家庭。我們的居民協會主席曾親自致函部長、提交完整的Crilly安全報告，而我們的處境亦已被《泰晤士報》、《金融時報》、BBC、CNN等多間媒體報導。英國民主問責制度何在？
The first duty of the UK government is to protect its citizens. We understand the UK’s diplomatic obligations - but not at the expense of its own people. The refusal to acknowledge the basic risks of housing a high-security foreign embassy on top of a residential block is deeply troubling. It appears the government is prioritising relations with Beijing over the safety of its own citizens.
英國政府的首要職責是保護其國民。我們明白外交義務，但不能以犧牲本國人民為代價。將一個高安全級別的外國大使館設於住宅區上方，而拒絕承認基本風險，是極度令人不安的。
It’s not just about us. Dissidents, including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese exile communities are terrified. They’ve told us they no longer feel safe protesting outside the site, and on British soil. Their presence, and ours, will be met with constant surveillance and intimidation by a regime known to harass and threaten activists - even abroad.
這件事不僅關係到我們。流亡港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人及中國異見社群皆感到恐懼。他們表示不再敢在該地點或英國土地上公開抗議。他們與我們一樣，將面對來自這個以恐嚇異見者聞名的政權的持續監控與威嚇。
The people have spoken, and they support us.
On 8 February 2025, thousands of British citizens - including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese pro-democracy activists, and human rights campaigners - gathered outside Royal Mint Court in protest against this embassy.
2025年2月8日，數以千計的英國公民 ，包括港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人、中國民主人士與人權倡議者， 齊集皇家鑄幣廠，抗議中國大使館計劃。
They were joined by cross-party MPs, journalists, and allies. Together, they said NO to the Chinese embassy, and YES to democratic values, safety, and justice.
他們與跨黨派議員、記者及盟友並肩站立，一同說出明確立場：反對中國大使館，支持民主、安全與公義。
Further mass protests followed on 15 March, 3 May, and 14 June - showing growing national resistance to the plan.
3月15日、5月3日及6月14日亦舉行後續大型集會，反對聲浪日益壯大。
They continue to protest, and have made it clear: they won’t stop until this mega-embassy deal is over.
抗議仍在持續，並清楚表示：他們不會停止，直至該項目取消為止。
But the Government is not listening.
But we need your help - fast.
The legal fees for a Judicial Review are beyond the reach of ordinary families. But with your help, we can stand up to both Beijing and Whitehall.
司法覆核的法律費用遠超普通家庭的負擔。但在您的幫助下，我們能夠與北京和英國政府對抗。
This case is about more than one building. It’s about:
Protecting British citizens from state overreach
Defending UK democracy from foreign influence
Challenging backroom deals that put power over people
If we succeed, we won’t just protect our homes. We’ll set a precedent that no foreign government can build on British soil without respecting British citizens and British values.
如若成功，我們不僅能保護我們的家園，我們更是創下先例：任何外國政府不得在罔顧英國公民和英國價值的前提下在英國土地上建造任何建築。
Please chip in whatever you can. £10. £100. £1,000. Every penny goes to legal costs to take this to court. We are a group of teachers, nurses, shop workers and pensioners. We don’t have the Chinese Communist Party’s millions - but with your help, we do have people power.
請您捐出任何您能負擔的金額 — 不論是 £10，£100 還是 £1,000。每一分錢都將用於支付法律費用，讓我們將此案帶上法庭。我們只是一群教師、護士、店員和退休人士。雖然我們沒有中國共產黨的龐大資金 — 但在您的幫助下，我們擁有的是人民的力量。
Because if they can do this to us, they can do it to anyone.
This is a secure UK-based platform, fully registered and subject to UK law.
It is widely used to support political and legal campaigns, including by MPs, NGOs, and grassroots movements - some of which are openly critical of the Chinese government.
該平台廣泛用於支持政治和法律活動，包括國會議員、非政府組織和基層運動 — 包括曾公開批評中國政府的政治活動。
The platform offers full transparency, with public donation records and payment processing via Stripe or PayPal.
該平台提供完全透明的捐款記錄，並通過 Stripe 或 PayPal 處理支付。
There is no history of censorship or compliance with pressure from the Chinese state.
It adheres strictly to GDPR regulations, ensuring donor and campaigner data is protected.
平台嚴格遵守 GDPR 規範，確保捐款者和活動者的數據安全。
2.95% + 0.25 of each donation goes to the platform; 100% of the remaining funds will be used to cover legal costs.
每筆捐款將扣除 2.95% 加 £0.25 之平台手續費，其餘款項將全數用以支付法律相關費用。
If the legal case is dismissed, your donation will be directed to charity unless you request a refund. If you would like your donation returned, please email us. We will calculate and refund your contribution (with platform fee deducted).
如法律訴訟最終被駁回，捐款將撥捐予慈善機構，除非閣下主動申請退款。如欲索回捐款，請電郵至，我們將在扣除平台手續費後，計算並退還閣下之捐款。

Fundraiser by Luke Rudkowski : Fund Independent Reporting In HONG KONG
Luke Rudkowski is organizing this fundraiser.
You know something big is happening in Hong Kong!! The protests have been massive, and they may be the biggest geopolitical event of the year. Will China get its way and stomp out dissent? Might covert U.S. aid allow the protesters to sustain their momentum? Needless to say, there is a lot at stake and lots of speculation!!
And because of that it’s important for there to be independent, on-the-ground reporting about the events in Hong Kong.
When massive Yellow Vests protests were taking place in Paris, We Are Change was there reporting on the ground and risking safety as protesters were losing eyes due to police brutality. In the past we have also been to places likeSomalia, Venezuela and Cheran , once the most violent, dangerous area in Mexico.
As for Hong Kong, it’s very expensive to fly and stay there. This mission will involve spending a week or more investigating, reporting and live-streaming.
So if you value reporting on the events in Hong Kong that is independent and free of spin and manipulation, then your support is crucial! By contributing to this campaign, you will help fund the cost of the flight, safety precautions and live reporting at events like the upcoming Civil Human Rights Front March on August 31 and the student strike that is set to take place on September 2, the first day of secondary school.
Our $2,700 goal is the bare minimum it will take to fund this trip. If we surpass the goal due to your support, which is so greatly appreciated, the funds will go toward other journalistic endeavors. Thank you so much! Your support means the world to us!

content:
Fundraiser by Kurshat Uyghur : Support Uyghur film & tell the story together
Kurshat Uyghur is organizing this fundraiser.
We've been making preparation for this film for nearly a year. It is a story of a young Uyghur man’s life in exile after losing contact with his family members. We have received funding from a few organizations, but not quite enough for the entire production process. So we decided to ask for help from those of you who care about the Uyghurs and the work that we’re doing. Our goal is to reach $10,000.
If you have any interest in Uyghur culture or the Uyghur film industry, then please consider a contribution. Your small act of kindness will greatly enhance this film, you will not be disappointed. This film will open your eyes to stories from a beautiful and marginalized people group
The film will be released on March 21st, 2023. All donors will be listed in the end credits and receive a steamable/ download link to the film, and donors who give $100 or more contributions will receive special thanks and additional gifts as shown below:
$100 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film and a handwritten thank you letter.
$200 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter.
$500 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter also your name will be present on the director's special thanks section ending of the film.
$5000 donation - you will receive all of the above and will be credited as a co-producer.
Shirzat, an Uyghur international student who has just graduated from college in the United States, had big dreams for his future prior to undertaking his education. He had planned to return to his homeland to take over his father's business, marry his long-term girlfriend, build a happy family, and become a successful entrepreneur. But with the sudden implementation of China's arbitrary mass abduction policy, millions of Uyghurs, like his father, were taken and have disappeared. For Shirzat, who wasn’t able to pursue his studies due to the crisis back home, this was tragic. He felt he had been thrown from the sky to the ground. With finances in ruins, his father missing, his family in danger, his relationship hanging by a thread, he soon spiraled into a cloud of depression and compulsive attention to politics. He withdrew from his relationships with his friends and put his life on hold while struggling to overcome his painful reality and searching for hope in the midst of it.
We will work with some of the most talented people around the world. The Director and screenwriter of this film have decades of experience in the industry. He has also made a number of short films while in university, many of which won the best picture of the year at regional and international film festivals. Our core team members are creative-minded people who have participated in numerous film projects. We have absolute confidence that we will work together as one and give the audiences astonishing results.
